title: Rome too confesses free choice before grace a slave of sin, and the beginning of justification from God alone
source_text: LIII. Vicissim vero manifestum fecimus Scholae Romanae Theologos cum Protestantibus fateri liberum hominis arbitrium, ante gratiam, sic esse peccati servum, ut nihil possit in iis in quibus vera & salutifera pietas in Deum consistit. Imo primum initium justificationis & conversionis nostrae a solo Deo esse, non vero a nostro libero arbitrio, & eo respectu hominem mere passive se habere.
pass_a_gloss: LIII. On the other hand we have made manifest that the Theologians of the Roman School confess with the Protestants that the free choice of man, before grace, is so the slave of sin, that it can do nothing in those things in which true and saving piety toward God consists. Nay that the first beginning of our justification and conversion is from God alone, not from our free choice, and in that respect man behaves merely passively.
pass_b_english: Conversely, we have shown that the theologians of the Roman School admit with the Protestants that man's free choice before grace is so enslaved to sin that it can do nothing in the things that make up true and saving piety toward God.
They even admit that the very beginning of our justification and conversion comes from God alone and not from our free choice, and that in this respect man is merely passive.
